name: NROL-136
destination_explanation: It starts around 160 km up and runs to about 2,000 km. At this height a satellite goes all the way around the planet in about an hour and a half.
slot_a_text: This is the 14th flight for B1097. It flies back to Landing Zone 4 rather than a drone ship. It last flew USSF-259 about 2 months ago.
slot_b_text: SpaceX's 129th launch of the year, 748th all time. It works out to a launch every other day. Falcon 9 is on a 349-flight success streak. Worldwide, it is attempt number 271 of the year.

lg_slot_b_text: It has already slipped twice. The current time was set in the last few hours and has held since. The window is only 30 minutes wide.

description: Fifteenth batch of satellites for a reconnaissance satellite constellation built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman for the National Reconnaissance Office to provide imaging and other reconnaissance capabilities.
rocket_fact: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is the first orbital class rocket capable of reflight.
